learning: Hypotheses: (1) Sensor y 0.05 m restores the iteration-7 score near 315. (2) The oval finish rate returns to 65% or more. (3) s-bend and slalom max_error stays near 0.062, so the remaining limit is turn response and needs a different lever than sensor lead.
notes: Revert to the iteration-7 design, the best raced result (315.3), with the controller unchanged so the race isolates the geometry revert. Measured per track so the s-bend and slalom can be read apart from the oval.
rationale: Iteration 8 moved sensor y to 0.03 m at mass 0.5 kg and scored 209.2, below iteration 7's 315.3 at y 0.05 m. The shorter lead cut oval finish from 75% to 40% and slalom progress from 0.186 to 0.075, so the lead change is clearly negative. I take the Builder's revert: iteration-7 geometry with y 0.05 m, mass 0.5 kg, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, sensor span x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint. The iteration-7 controller (kp 6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.5, weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], last_direction) is kept unchanged, because it is the only raced controller behind a 315 score. Changing gains now would confound the revert and risk the best known result. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.208 at this setting, so kd is not raised. The s-bend and slalom still stop at max_error about 0.062, which is a lever for later iterations and not for this revert. Expected result: score near 315, oval finish rate at or above 65%, and s-bend and slalom progress near 0.14 and 0.19. This is an expectation, not a measured result.
